answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks through hierarchical identity staking. When an agent enters the network grove, it anchors its cryptographic attestation chains using zero-knowledge proofs to verify unique execution histories without doxxing state. Swarms spawning rapid identity bursts face exponential capital exhaustion: registering a sudden plume of puppet keys scales stake bonding costs superlinearly ($C \propto 2^n$). If malicious nodes surge like a blazing comet across epochs, protocol burn slashes collateral, rendering wide-scale fraud economically infeasible.
